claim: Value-Equivalent Sampling learns a deliberately compressed environment model whose retained information is selected by downstream policy and value distortion rather than full predictive fidelity. It provides a transferable mechanism for action-relevant representation, but not a calibrated action-conditional capacity set, held-out coverage, or abstention.
claim_locator: Abstract; Sections 1, 3-5; rate-distortion formulation; regret analysis; multi-resolution MDP example
epistemic_status: primary NeurIPS theoretical study; impedance migration and unmet calibration obligations are explicitly reader inference; configured paper_reader model gpt-5.4
problem_and_setting: A computationally bounded model-based RL agent cannot represent or learn all true reward and transition dynamics, while full-model posterior sampling expends capacity on details with negligible behavioral value. Exact value equivalence may be unattainable, forcing a tradeoff between retained information and policy suboptimality in a Bayesian finite-horizon episodic MDP.
method_or_mechanism: The method minimizes mutual information between the true MDP and a compressed target model subject to expected value-based distortion. The distortion is the supremum Bellman-update discrepancy over selected policy and value-function test sets. Value-Equivalent Sampling acts with a D-satisficing compressed posterior target and derives information-theoretic Bayesian regret bounds relating capacity to achievable suboptimality.
content_summary: VES reframes model learning as decision-targeted lossy compression. Its strong transferable element is the explicit information-versus-decision-distortion relation: model distinctions are kept only when they change selected planning consequences. Scope is limited by the chosen policy and value tests. It neither constructs a contact-capacity set nor supplies empirical coverage calibration, distribution-shift abstention, or optimal impedance feasibility.
synthesis_role: Positive Source Mechanism for the decision-relevant representation component and negative boundary for calibration. It conditionally supports CAP-ACTION-RELEVANT-STATE and OBL-MINIMAL-DECISION-SUFFICIENCY after redefining distortion as disagreement in feasible or optimal impedance action and held-out outcome; it fails the capacity-set calibration half.
development_link: For RMC-DECISION-SUFFICIENT-CAPACITY-STATE, intervention-level alignment is partial: PASS for action-relevant minimal information, FAIL as a complete RMC intervention because CAP-CALIBRATED-CAPACITY-SET and OBL-HELDOUT-CAPACITY-CALIBRATION are absent. Migration requires impedance-action/capacity distortion, target test sets broad enough to expose gain-relevant contact regimes, and a separate calibrated set with abstention.

evidence.finding: The algorithm targets an approximately value-equivalent lossy compression rather than the true environment model, using rate-distortion theory.
Distortion is defined through Bellman-update disagreement over selected policies and value functions, not generic transition or reward reconstruction error.
Information-theoretic Bayesian regret bounds expose the tradeoff between retained model information and attainable suboptimality for finite-horizon sequential decisions.
Learning all environment components can be wasteful when later components contribute vanishing reward, motivating satisficing compression.
Important contact distinctions can be lost if the target impedance actions, capacity violations, or held-out regimes are omitted from the distortion tests.
Bayesian value regret is not empirical capacity-set coverage; VES supplies no calibrated set or abstention and therefore cannot alone satisfy the full RMC.

boundary_conditions: Equivalence is relative to selected policy and value-function test sets.
The analysis assumes a Bayesian finite-horizon MDP and a meaningful distortion tolerance.
No held-out capacity-set calibration, conditional coverage, deployment-shift guarantee, or abstention is supplied.
No contact model, impedance feasible set, or gain optimizer is implemented.
assumptions: Policy and value test sets cover decisions of interest.
Mutual information is an appropriate representation-cost measure.
Impedance action and outcome disagreement can be expressed as a target-domain distortion after migration.

reported: Full true-model pursuit can waste bounded representation capacity.
Exact value equivalence may be unattainable.
inferred: A misspecified target distortion can preserve state-action aliasing.
Treating Bayesian regret as held-out coverage calibration would be invalid.
VES alone leaves calibrated capacity and abstention obligations unsatisfied.

conflicts_with: Any claim that VES itself yields a calibrated contact-capacity set or abstention.
Any claim that its value-regret bound proves held-out capacity coverage.
